hook.text: Peter and Rosemary Grant spent 40 years on a tiny Galápagos island watching finches evolve in real time.

buildup.text: During a 1977 drought, large-beaked finches survived because they could crack tough seeds.

discovery.text: The Grants documented natural selection happening year by year—something Darwin could only infer from fossils.

twist.text: When rains returned, small beaks bounced back. Selection reversed. Evolution isn't a one-way street—it oscillates.

climax.text: In 2015, they found the gene responsible: ALX1. Decades of observation met molecular proof. The puzzle completed.

punchline.text: Darwin imagined it. The Grants watched it happen.

quiz.question: What gene controls finch beak shape?
